verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch is targeted for April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Launch is targeted for no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT Wednesday, April 1'; R3: 'NASA is targeting a Wednesday, April 1 launch'; R6: 'tomorrow, April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the target launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch can be viewed live on NASA+ beginning around 7:45 a.m. EDT.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: '12:50 p.m.: NASA+ coverage of launch begins'; R3: '12:50 p.m. ET: Coverage... begins on NASA+'; R6: 'NASA+ coverage... beginning at 12:50 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify NASA+ coverage starts at 12:50 p.m. EDT, not 7:45 a.m., directly contradicting the claimed start time.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch can be viewed live on NASA’s YouTube channel beginning around 7:45 a.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '7:45 a.m.: Coverage of tanking operations... begins'; R3: '7:45 a.m. ET: Views and commentary on YouTube'; R6: 'YouTube coverage begins Wednesday at 7:45 a.m. EDT with tanking operations'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm YouTube coverage starts at 7:45 a.m. EDT for tanking operations.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 launch can be viewed live on Amazon Prime Video beginning around 7:45 a.m. EDT.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Watch... on NASA+ and Amazon Prime' (no specific time); R3: 'Livestreams... on... Amazon Prime... throughout the day' (no 7:45); R9: 'NASA+ content... on Prime Video... under Prime's Live TV'
verifications.reasoning: Amazon Prime carries NASA+ content, which starts at 12:50 p.m., not 7:45 a.m.; no source supports 7:45 start time for Prime.

verifications.claim: NASA+ and YouTube provide continuous coverage of the Artemis 2 launch starting with tanking operations at 7:45 a.m. EDT.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R6: 'YouTube coverage begins... at 7:45 a.m.... continuously... NASA+... beginning at 12:50 p.m.'; R3: '7:45 a.m.... on YouTube... 12:50 p.m.... on NASA+'
verifications.reasoning: YouTube starts continuous at 7:45 a.m., but NASA+ starts later at 12:50 p.m., contradicting joint continuous coverage from 7:45.

verifications.claim: NASA+ and YouTube provide more curated, shorter coverage of the Artemis 2 launch starting at 12:50 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R6: 'NASA+ coverage is a shorter, more curated broadcast, beginning at 12:50 p.m. EDT' (YouTube continuous from 7:45); R2: '12:50 p.m.: NASA+ coverage... Coverage continues on YouTube after...'
verifications.reasoning: Only NASA+ is described as curated/shorter at 12:50 p.m.; YouTube is continuous from earlier, contradicting attribution to both.

verifications.claim: The NASA App allows streaming of the Artemis 2 launch directly on iOS, Android, Roku, and Fire TV.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'NASA+ is available on iOS, Android... Roku, Apple TV, and Fire TV'; 'NASA App... unlocks access to... NASA+ streaming service'
verifications.reasoning: NASA App provides NASA+ streaming, explicitly available on listed platforms.

verifications.claim: Amazon Prime Video provides live coverage of the Artemis 2 launch under the Prime "Live TV" section.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R9: 'Viewers can find it under Prime's Live TV section at the top of the screen when they open the app'
verifications.reasoning: Source directly states NASA content on Prime Video under 'Live TV' section.

verifications.claim: In-person viewing of the Artemis 2 launch is available on Florida's Space Coast.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Best Central Florida locations... Brevard County (the Space Coast)'; R7: 'Florida’s Space Coast'; R8: 'see the launch... on the Space Coast'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm viewing spots on Florida's Space Coast.

verifications.claim: Official watch parties for the Artemis 2 launch are held at Space Center Houston.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R11: 'Artemis II Launch Watch Party... at Space Center Houston... live broadcast of the Artemis II launch'
verifications.reasoning: Source directly describes official watch party event at Space Center Houston.

verifications.claim: Space View Park, Parrish Park, and Sand Point Park are popular spots for in-person viewing in Titusville on Florida's Space Coast.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'TITUSVILLE... SPACE VIEW PARK... SAND POINT PARK... PARRISH PARK'; R8: 'Space View Park... Sand Point Park... Parrish Park'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly list these exact parks in Titusville as viewing spots.

verifications.claim: Jetty Park Pier, Alan Shepard Park, and Lori Wilson Park are in-person viewing spots in Cocoa Beach/Cape Canaveral on Florida's Space Coast.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Sources directly list these parks as viewing spots in the specified areas.
